cells.tense: Here, with the pen, the route you hand over comes from thinking you have actually done.
cells.act: make something skilled and small on the cleared ground
cells.ask: Form a version of what you've worked out — a page, a sample, a rough draft — and put it in front of the one person crossing the same gap. No deadline.
cells.core: You can think a thing through and then hand the route to somebody else, a clear path shaped by your own careful work rather than borrowed. It sits in a seed state: more than one direction is still open and none has collapsed. Nothing committed means it can feel like there is nothing to show yet. That is the bend — the sharing waits on a decision that hasn't been made, and the waiting can dress itself up as more preparation. So form a piece of it on ground you've already cleared, out of what you know rather than what you are still learning, and put it in front of the one person trying to cross where you crossed. It does not need to be finished or good. It needs to exist, so the route stops living only in your head.
cells.sheetLine: The way through is in your head. Put a piece of it out.
cells.verb: steering a way through for others
cells.place: a seed state before things have split apart

cells.tense: Soon, you will be forcing a route before anything has shown you the actual passage.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Go at the part you keep circling — on purpose, no outcome riding on it. Stay with it long enough to find out what holds when you stop forcing the passage open.
cells.core: You will be bracing for a future that can't be written in yet, and the direction you give people will harden before it lands — a held map rather than a walked route. Reading the crossing is not the problem; that part works. What is coming is treating the uncertainty as the enemy, pushing the answer out ahead of its time so the people following get told where to step before the ground has been checked. Underneath it, a practice can flow without force — solitude connecting instead of isolating. So take the hard part you keep circling and go at it, on purpose, with nothing riding on the result. Not to solve it. To see what stands when you stop shoving. What is false in the method drops; the commitment stays.

cells.tense: A door already closed behind you, and you have been standing at it, still looking through.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: Let your own sense of what's right settle a small undecided matter, before the reasoning talks you back out of the answer you already have.
cells.core: You used to chart the way for people; now the route you would give yourself has gone quiet, and standing before any choice feels less like possibility and more like fog. A door closed behind you and your body is still facing it. Underneath, a practice is yours and nobody else's, and it hasn't gone anywhere — it just isn't being asked. So let your own private sense of what's right settle a small undecided thing, the one you keep rechecking, and do it before the reasoning carries you off. You don't need to see the whole route for that one. It has been in your hand the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: The door closed behind you. Your own compass didn't.

cells.tense: You are steering people's thinking toward clear water while telling yourself you are only standing nearby.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Pick one person already in the same work and run a single piece of it out loud together, instead of handling it quietly on your own.
cells.core: The direction is being given — your careful thinking is charting real passage for the people near you — and your own account has it as something that just happened. The doing is real. The name on it is blank. Being in a seed state makes that easier to miss, because nothing has been committed to, so it feels like there is nothing to claim. So pick one person already in the same work and do a piece of it out loud with them, the two of you, rather than running it silently. Nothing changes in what you do, and the work stops happening only elsewhere. You watch your own hand steer, once.
cells.sheetLine: You show the way and say you're not the one steering.

attempts.check: The record supports that Potential — pure possibility before differentiation — is a seed stage and that Guidance's outer face is Cognition, disciplined thinking serving others, but it does not place any particular person on a bridge in their life; that is my reading, not in the record. A reader could say the card is about a stage of a project or a role, not a boat crossing water. The ask survives my being wrong: in any reading, building one small new thing from cleared ground still teaches something about disciplined thinking. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you know things other people need,' which is a flattering universal rather than something the record earned.
